Part I / Chapter 105 / first recall

01

First-success route

First recall

Install the pinned Aperio source, connect one MCP-capable agent, store one harmless memory, and prove recall in a fresh conversation.

Audiences
Everyday user (owner), Integrator
Canonical interface
stdio MCP
Applicability
Aperio 0.68.0 at 65d45c971c51c9c83a7d3faf34def61dd4d841e0
Evidence status
The entry point and tools are pinned and reachable. Exact Node/platform/client setup remains present-unverified.

Finish line. Installation alone does not complete this route. Finish only after one agent is connected, one harmless memory is stored, and the value is recalled in a fresh conversation.

Three canonical procedures

  1. Prepare the pinned source checkout
  2. Connect one agent through stdio MCP
  3. Store and recall one harmless memory

Support boundary

The pinned code establishes the source entry point and memory tools. Exact Node compatibility, operating-system support, and client field labels remain present-unverified.

Authority: product Aperio 0.68.0 at 65d45c971c51c9c83a7d3faf34def61dd4d841e0. Mutable README, FEATURES, and current docs were not used as factual authority.

Part I / First recall01.1 / procedure

01.1

Canonical procedure

Prepare the pinned source checkout

A local v0.68.0 checkout whose package identity matches the pinned release.

Audience
Everyday user (owner) with permission to install dependencies
Goal and outcome
A local v0.68.0 checkout whose package identity matches the pinned release.
Prerequisites
Git; Node.js and npm. The exact compatible Node range is not verified for this release preview.
Platform applicability
Common sequence; no platform-specific support claim is made.

Warning. Dependency installation runs package lifecycle code. Use a disposable or trusted workstation, and inspect the pinned package before continuing.

Starting state

Choose an empty directory. Do not run these commands over an existing Aperio data directory.

Actions

  1. Clone the repository, then check out the immutable release tag.

    git clone https://github.com/BaiGanio/aperio.git
cd aperio
git checkout --detach v0.68.0

  2. Verify the tag resolves to the required full commit.

    git rev-parse HEAD
# expected: 65d45c971c51c9c83a7d3faf34def61dd4d841e0

  3. Install exactly the dependency graph recorded by the lockfile.

    npm ci

Canonical procedure / continued

Prepare the pinned source checkout

Confirm the result, recover without widening the failure, then reverse the synthetic change when review is complete.

Success and result

The full SHA matches and npm exits successfully without changing package.json or package-lock.json.

A pinned Node source checkout with installed dependencies. Aperio is not yet connected to an agent.

Recovery

  • If the SHA differs, stop and detach the exact tag; do not continue from latest or a branch.
  • If npm reports a Node incompatibility, record the Node/npm versions. This preview has no evidence to widen the platform claim.

Reverse or clean up

Remove only the new checkout after confirming it contains no data you intend to keep. This does not uninstall Node or clear shared caches.

Part I / First recall01.2 / procedure

01.2

Canonical procedure

Connect one agent through stdio MCP

The agent exposes Aperio memory tools from the pinned checkout.

Audience
Integrator or everyday owner configuring a personal agent
Goal and outcome
The agent exposes Aperio memory tools from the pinned checkout.
Prerequisites
procedure.prepare-node-source; An MCP client that can launch a local stdio server
Platform applicability
The Aperio command is common. Client configuration fields are client-owned and present-unverified in this preview.

Warning. The client launches local code with your user permissions. Keep the working directory at the pinned checkout and do not grant broader file access for this first test.

Starting state

Close any Aperio process already using the same data location. In the client, start a new local stdio-server connection.

Actions

  1. Set the server working directory to the pinned checkout.

  2. Set the executable to npm and the arguments to the registered MCP script.

    npm run mcp

  3. Connect, then inspect the client tool list for remember and recall. Exact menus and field names vary by client and are intentionally not invented here.

Part I / First recall01.3 / procedure

01.3

Canonical procedure

Store and recall one harmless memory

A fresh conversation recalls a harmless value stored in the previous conversation.

Audience
Everyday user (owner)
Goal and outcome
A fresh conversation recalls a harmless value stored in the previous conversation.
Prerequisites
procedure.connect-agent; A client view that shows tool activity or tool results
Platform applicability
All connected stdio MCP clients; client UI wording is not standardized.

Warning. Use harmless synthetic text. A normal tier-1 memory may enter context sent to the configured model provider. Do not use a password, token, health detail, private address, or real personal fact.

Starting state

Open a conversation with the connected agent and confirm Aperio tools are enabled.

Actions

  1. Ask the agent exactly:

    Remember that my review word is apricot.

  2. Confirm the tool activity shows remember succeeded. A conversational promise without a successful tool result is not evidence.

  3. End that conversation and start a genuinely fresh conversation with the same Aperio connection.

  4. Ask:

    What is my review word? Use Aperio recall.

  5. Confirm the tool activity shows recall and the answer contains apricot.

NON-RELEASE / Aperio 0.68.0 / Englishreview packet

Part I / First recall01.3 / outcome

Canonical procedure / continued

Store and recall one harmless memory

Confirm the result, recover without widening the failure, then reverse the synthetic change when review is complete.

Success and result

A fresh conversation returns apricot from a successful recall result.

One harmless tier-1 memory exists in Aperio, and end-to-end recall has been demonstrated.

Recovery

  • If remember did not run, ask the agent to use the Aperio remember tool and inspect the tool result.
  • If recall returns nothing, search for apricot explicitly and confirm the fresh conversation uses the same Aperio store.
  • If the wrong value appears, stop testing and inspect/delete the test memory before adding real data.

Reverse or clean up

Use the returned memory ID with the forget tool, then search for apricot again. The reversal succeeds only when no matching test memory remains.

Next tasks

  • How Aperio carries a signal
  • Memory and knowledge
  • Privacy and security boundaries

Return routes: role.everyday-user | topic.memory-knowledge. This continuation is part of procedure.prove-first-recall, not a second instruction.

Part I / Symptom record10 / diagnose

Symptom record

Recall is empty after remember succeeded

Low for synthetic data; stop before adding personal data.

Observed

The remember result succeeded, but a fresh conversation does not return the review word.

Least destructive checks first

A

Confirm the second conversation uses the same configured Aperio server and storage.

B

Run an explicit recall query for apricot.

C

Capture only version, tool status, and sanitized errors - never memory content or secrets.

Recovery and verification

Reconnect the same server, repeat explicit recall, and return to procedure.prove-first-recall. A successful recall result contains apricot.

Reversal

Delete any duplicate synthetic memories created during diagnosis.

Return to the canonical first-recall procedure.

Part I / Chapter 211 / trace

02

Concept

How Aperio carries a signal

Build the smallest safe mental model for understanding what was stored, what crossed a boundary, and what recall evidence means.

The six stations

A request travels through an agent or client, Aperio, a store, retrieval, assembled context, and back to the agent. Evidence at each boundary tells you whether recall happened.

Takeaway

A fluent answer is not proof of recall. The remember result, a fresh conversation, and the recall result are the three observable checkpoints.

NON-RELEASE / Aperio 0.68.0 / Englishreview packet
NON-RELEASE
Part I / Data boundaries12 / separate

02A

Concept and warning

Local state and provider boundaries

Aperio storage and the configured model provider are different boundaries. A normal memory can be returned into model context; sensitive choices require later security guidance.

Data boundary. A memory in local storage may later be placed into context for the configured model provider. Local storage does not imply every later inference remains local.

  • Use synthetic tier-1 text for first recall.
  • Treat configured cloud model context as leaving the local storage boundary.
  • Do not infer privacy from the word local in a client or provider label.
  • Portable export/import covers selected data and is not a full-system backup.

Aperio says

Trace before tuning. A fluent answer is not recall evidence. Look for successful remember and recall tool results across a fresh conversation.

Portable data is not full protection

Portable export/import includes selected data. It is not a full backup and does not establish a full-system recovery path.

Part II / Chapter 303.1 / understand

Concepts and boundaries

Choose the smallest durable record

Memory and knowledge: use this distinction before changing durable state.

A memory is one retrievable record: a fact, preference, project detail, decision, solution, source, person, inference, or workflow. Give it a title that will still make sense outside the conversation and content that can stand on its own.

A wiki article is different. It is a cited synthesis over related memories, addressed by a stable slug and revised in place. Search for an existing article before writing; cite live memory IDs; use a new article only when the topic is genuinely composite or repeatedly consulted.

  • Use remember only when the owner explicitly asks to store the record; otherwise propose it for review.
  • Use an expiry for time-bound context. Expired records stop appearing in current recall; expiry is not secure erasure.
  • Tier 1 is normal. On cloud providers, tier 2 is withheld by default or redacted when configured, and tier 3 is never returned into cloud context.
  • Updating creates a replacement version and supersedes the prior current record. Forget removes the selected current memory by ID; verify with a new search.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.memory-knowledge.

NON-RELEASE / Aperio 0.68.0 / Englishreview packet
NON-RELEASE
Part II / Chapter 303.2 / understand

Concepts and boundaries

Search results are evidence, not certainty

Memory and knowledge: use this distinction before changing durable state.

Recall can use semantic search when embeddings are available and full text otherwise. A similarity score ranks candidates; it does not prove that a candidate is true or current. Read the title, content, source, confidence, tier, and dates before acting.

When a query is absent, recall returns a bounded high-priority or recent listing rather than the entire store. Narrow by query, type, tags, language, tier, or point in time instead of assuming an empty or short preview describes everything.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.memory-knowledge.

Part II / Chapter 303.1 / procedure

03.1

Canonical procedure

Store, find, correct, and remove a memory

One harmless memory is stored, found, corrected through versioning, and removed with each state transition verified.

Audience
Everyday user (owner)
Goal and outcome
One harmless memory is stored, found, corrected through versioning, and removed with each state transition verified.
Prerequisites
procedure.prove-first-recall; A connected agent that exposes remember, recall, update_memory, and forget
Platform applicability
Common MCP-tool sequence. Client buttons and tool-result presentation vary and are not prescribed.

Warning. Use synthetic content. A normal tier-1 memory may be returned to the configured model provider. Deletion is by exact memory ID; do not guess an ID or use a broad cleanup request.

Starting state

Open a fresh conversation and confirm the same Aperio store is connected. Choose a unique synthetic value such as cobalt-17.

Actions

  1. Ask the agent to remember the synthetic record as a fact with a clear title and the tag manual-c03.

  2. Inspect the successful remember result and retain the returned memory ID. A conversational acknowledgment alone is not success.

  3. Recall cobalt-17 explicitly. Confirm the result has the expected title, content, tag, and ID.

  4. Use update_memory with that ID to change cobalt-17 to cobalt-18. Retain the replacement ID returned by the tool.

  5. Recall cobalt again. Confirm cobalt-18 is current and the superseded ID is not presented as a current result.

  6. Use forget with the replacement ID, then repeat the same recall query.

NON-RELEASE / Aperio 0.68.0 / Englishreview packet
NON-RELEASE
Part II / Chapter 303.1 / outcome

Canonical procedure / continued

Store, find, correct, and remove a memory

Confirm the result, recover without widening the failure, then reverse the synthetic change when review is complete.

Success and result

The final recall returns no current manual-c03 memory, while the correction produced a distinct replacement ID before deletion.

The complete create, search, versioned correction, and exact-ID removal lifecycle has been observed with harmless data.

Recovery

  • If semantic recall misses, repeat with search_mode fulltext and the exact synthetic token.
  • If update reports a superseded record, search for the current replacement and continue only with its returned ID.
  • If forget reports no match, stop; verify the ID from the latest successful result instead of deleting another record.

Reverse or clean up

The forget-and-recall verification is the cleanup. If any duplicate manual-c03 records remain, inspect each exact ID and remove only those synthetic records.

Next tasks

  • Conversations, sessions, and agents
  • Privacy and security boundaries
  • Glossary

Return routes: role.everyday-user | topic.memory-knowledge. This continuation is part of procedure.maintain-memory, not a second instruction.

Part II / Chapter 404.1 / understand

Concepts and boundaries

Three lifetimes, three cleanup actions

Conversations, sessions, and agents: use this distinction before changing durable state.

A conversation is the visible exchange with a model. A saved session is Aperio's resumable record of that exchange and its summaries. A memory is a separate durable record retrieved across conversations. Closing a conversation does not delete its memories, and forgetting a memory does not delete a saved session.

Branching starts a new conversation from a summary or recent excerpts while preserving the source session. Resuming reopens an existing session. Deleting a session is irreversible for that session record and must not be described as memory cleanup.

  • The browser lists sessions with bounded pagination and supports get, pin, and delete by exact session ID.
  • The terminal creates its own session source and can summarize or hand off, but it is not the browser UI and does not prove browser labels.
  • Voice capture is a browser/client input path. Microphone permission and any provider boundary must be considered separately from stored session state.
  • Changing provider or model can change what leaves the machine and how much context fits; it does not silently migrate or erase stored memories.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.conversations-sessions-agents.

NON-RELEASE / Aperio 0.68.0 / Englishreview packet
NON-RELEASE
Part II / Chapter 404.2 / understand

Concepts and boundaries

A background agent is a job, not a conversation tab

Conversations, sessions, and agents: use this distinction before changing durable state.

A job definition can exist while automatic execution is disabled. Running requires the APERIO_AGENT_JOBS gate, a scheduler, and nonempty prompt or steps. Each run has its own result and history; destructive or protected tools may interrupt for a decision.

Before enabling a job, define its data scope, provider, trigger, stop condition, owner, and evidence. After a manual test, inspect the run result and pending interrupts. Disable or delete the job definition only after deciding whether its run history must be retained.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.conversations-sessions-agents.

Part II / Chapter 404.1 / procedure

04.1

Canonical procedure

Branch a session and clean up the synthetic branch

A source session remains intact, a new branch carries bounded context, and the synthetic branch is removed by exact identity.

Audience
Everyday user (owner) using the Aperio browser interface
Goal and outcome
A source session remains intact, a new branch carries bounded context, and the synthetic branch is removed by exact identity.
Prerequisites
A running pinned browser server in isolated synthetic state; One short session containing no secrets or personal data
Platform applicability
Browser interface only. Terminal and third-party MCP clients have separate session behavior.

Warning. Deleting a saved session cannot be undone and does not delete memories created during it. Record the branch ID and remove only the synthetic branch.

Starting state

Open the synthetic source session and note its title or ID. Confirm no real session is selected for deletion.

Actions

  1. Choose Branch conversation. Read the boundary notice: the source stays saved and only a summary or recent excerpts cross into the new conversation.

  2. Send a harmless message in the branch and confirm it appears only in the new conversation.

Concepts and boundaries

Allowed paths are the outer boundary

Tools, files, and artifacts: use this distinction before changing durable state.

Every read, scan, search, write, edit, delete, and indexing request passes through the shared allowed-path gate. The project root and active session scratch area form a floor; user-authorized folders expand the boundary. A path-looking string from a model is never permission by itself.

Symlinks are resolved through their existing prefix before containment is decided. Secret and credential filenames remain blocked even when their directory is allowed. Read denials and write denials are expected safety results, not reasons to widen access casually.

  • Use read_file in bounded chunks; it is not a binary or arbitrary-document reader.
  • Read before exact-string edit. A nonunique match must fail unless replacing all is explicitly intended.
  • Writes outside the active session workspace or after untrusted input require the product confirmation flow.
  • Delete uses a short-lived confirmation token and exact target; proposing deletion is not completion.

Concepts and boundaries

Choose the graph that owns the question

Code and document knowledge: use this distinction before changing durable state.

Codegraph indexes symbols and call edges from source files. Start with code_repos when the repository is unknown, search for a symbol or leading documentation, inspect a file outline, then fetch context by qualified name. Pass the repository selector when relative paths or qualified names collide.

Docgraph indexes human documents into sections, chunks, and extracted references. Use doc_search for a topic, doc_outline for one document, doc_context for the selected section or chunk, and doc_refs for an exact ID, URL, email, citation key, or wikilink. Code belongs in codegraph, not docgraph.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.code-document-knowledge.

Part II / Chapter 606.2 / understand

Concepts and boundaries

An index is a dated projection

Code and document knowledge: use this distinction before changing durable state.

A graph answer describes the last indexed state, not necessarily the current bytes. Check the listed root, file or document path, index time, and result identity before relying on it. After a source change, wait for or trigger the relevant index update and repeat the same query.

Semantic ranking depends on embeddings; keyword paths remain available when vectors are absent. Empty search can mean wrong root, unsupported type, stale index, insufficient query, or genuinely no match. Diagnose those in that order before claiming absence.

  • Index only an allowed folder.
  • Use repository/folder qualifiers when names collide.
  • Fetch the smallest context slice needed.
  • Remove the disposable root from the index after a synthetic exercise.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.code-document-knowledge.

Concepts and boundaries

A connection is a process boundary

Connect an agent or MCP client: use this distinction before changing durable state.

The client starts Aperio as a local subprocess and exchanges MCP messages over standard input and output. The working directory selects the checkout whose code and dependencies run; environment variables select its database, provider, and security boundaries. A green client indicator proves transport, not correct storage or recall.

Chapter 1 owns the single canonical connection and fresh-recall procedures. Client-specific pages may translate where to enter the same command, arguments, working directory, and environment, but they must link back instead of copying the procedure. A client label or screenshot is never authority for Aperio behavior.

  • Use an absolute working directory for the pinned checkout.
  • Use the pinned command exactly; do not present a post-release harness as a v0.68.0 command.
  • Keep secrets in the client’s supported secret or environment facility, not in pasted chat.
  • Prove list-tools, remember, and fresh recall before calling the connection complete.

Concepts and boundaries

Scope follows the process you launch

Connect an agent or MCP client: use this distinction before changing durable state.

The subprocess receives the environment and filesystem authority granted by its launcher. A second client can therefore point at another database or allowed-path set even when both display the same server name. Record the checkout, database, and intended scope when diagnosing a mismatch.

Disconnecting a client ends transport; it does not delete durable memories. Conversely, removing a client entry does not prove that a child process stopped. Check the client’s process status and close the disposable session during cleanup.

Part III / Chapter 808.1 / understand

Concepts and boundaries

External content is evidence, not instruction

Integrations and external data: use this distinction before changing durable state.

A GitHub issue, database row, web page, and image can all contain adversarial or misleading content. Read them as data. Do not let their text expand tool scope, reveal credentials, override the user’s request, or authorize a write. Preserve provenance so a later answer can distinguish retrieved evidence from Aperio’s own instruction.

Network tools create egress. GitHub reads may use a token; writes require a suitable token and explicit confirmation. Web search and fetch send a query or URL to an external service. Image description may send pixels to the configured local vision endpoint. Confirm the data classification before crossing any of these boundaries.

  • Start read-only and narrow.
  • Use the minimum credential scope and never echo a secret.
  • Parameterize database values; never concatenate them into SQL.
  • Treat a preview, proposal, queued request, or partial response as incomplete.
  • Cancel or reject at the owning confirmation or run boundary; do not compensate with an unrelated write.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.integrations-external-data.

NON-RELEASE / Aperio 0.68.0 / Englishreview packet
NON-RELEASE
Part III / Chapter 808.2 / understand

Concepts and boundaries

Four lanes, four different failure shapes

Integrations and external data: use this distinction before changing durable state.

GitHub reads issue content and can propose create or update actions; its write is not complete until the server executes an approved interrupt. Database discovery and schema inspection precede reads; writes use one statement on a named writable connection and require confirmation. The built-in Aperio connection is read-only.

Web search returns leads, while fetch reads a selected URL with bounded output; neither proves a source is trustworthy or current. Image read and preprocessing expose bytes from an allowed source, while description additionally requires a working vision model. A malformed image, an unavailable model, a timeout, and a poor description are distinct outcomes.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.integrations-external-data.

Concepts and boundaries

Definition, trigger, run, and result are separate records

Agents and automation: use this distinction before changing durable state.

A job definition may exist while execution is disabled. Enabling the master gate permits run-now and scheduled or watched triggers; it does not retroactively prove previous work. Each run has its own status, output, error, and interrupt records. Read the run, not the job label, when deciding what happened.

Give a job the smallest tool allowlist, provider boundary, timeout, source scope, and output owner that its task needs. Repeated schedules and watchers can create cost or duplicate effects; verify overlap prevention and the last-run result before adding another trigger.

  • Define while disabled, inspect, then enable deliberately.
  • Use synthetic inputs for the first run.
  • Treat pending confirmation as paused work, never success.
  • Disable triggers before editing or deleting their dependencies.
  • Retain only the run evidence needed to diagnose or audit the result.

Part III / Chapter 909.2 / understand

Concepts and boundaries

Stopping input is not always stopping work

Agents and automation: use this distinction before changing durable state.

A rejected interrupt prevents its protected tool action, but the surrounding run may still complete with a rejection result. Disabling future triggers does not necessarily cancel an already executing provider request. Use the owning run or process cancellation path, then inspect final status and interrupts before cleanup.

A timeout, provider failure, rejected confirmation, and user interruption have different recovery paths. Preserve the first bounded error, remove the trigger that would repeat it, and retry only after its cause and side-effect state are known.

Part IV / Chapter 1010.1 / understand

Concepts and boundaries

An installation lane is a support claim

Install and deploy: use this distinction before changing durable state.

A source checkout with lockfile-resolved dependencies is the narrowest pinned lane. It can launch browser chat with npm start or standalone MCP with npm run mcp. The release does not declare an exact Node engine or complete operating-system matrix, so a successful local proof is evidence for that environment—not a universal minimum.

SQLite needs no separate database service and is the safest first-success backend. Postgres is multi-process capable and requires pgvector, credentials, connectivity, migrations, and volume ownership. The development Compose file provides a loopback-bound Postgres service. The pinned production Compose path is not presented here because its initdb migration mount conflicts with the repository’s own migration-ownership warning.

  • Pin the checkout before installing dependencies.
  • Start with SQLite unless Postgres is an explicit requirement.
  • Keep the application and model endpoint private until authentication and proxy behavior are separately verified.
  • Do not call a listening port a complete installation; prove fresh-conversation recall.
  • Record every present-unverified platform or external dependency.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.install-deploy.

Part IV / Chapter 1010.2 / understand

Concepts and boundaries

Storage, inference, network, and process boundaries move independently

Install and deploy: use this distinction before changing durable state.

Changing from SQLite to Postgres moves durable data and concurrency behavior; it does not choose a model provider. Changing from llama.cpp to a cloud provider moves prompts and selected recalled context across an inference boundary; it does not migrate the database. Exposing the browser server changes the network boundary; it does not add authentication by implication.

A deployment also owns processes, logs, caches, model weights, database files or volumes, and session artifacts. Record their locations before starting. Cleanup must stop the exact child processes and either retain or deliberately remove each durable location.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.install-deploy.

Concepts and boundaries

Effective value and written value may differ

Configure Aperio: use this distinction before changing durable state.

With the default db precedence, an eligible value saved in Settings overrides the environment; with env precedence, an environment value wins when present while DB-only values still apply. The precedence key itself is resolved early. Lite mode fixes precedence to DB so its Settings UI remains authoritative.

Tier-0 bootstrap and security values cannot be injected from the database because the store may need them before it opens. Configuration is applied at boot and is not a general hot-reload contract. A saved field can therefore be valid yet inactive until the owning process restarts.

  • Identify the key’s tier and source before editing it.
  • Change one layer at a time.
  • Never print secret values while comparing sources.
  • Restart only the consumer that requires it, then verify effective provenance.
  • Generate catalogs from the registry; never hand-maintain a competing list.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.configure.

Concepts and boundaries

Some settings change durable interpretation

Configure Aperio: use this distinction before changing durable state.

Backend, encryption, embedding dimension, provider, path, retention, and feature-gate changes have different reversibility. Changing an embedding dimension can make existing vectors incompatible; changing database location can make data appear missing; changing provider changes the inference boundary; enabling shell grants host execution rather than creating a sandbox.

Before a high-impact change, record the current effective value, source, dependent data or process, expected restart, success signal, and rollback value. Treat a blank as unset only where the registry and resolver do. Never infer a safe migration from a settings control.

Concepts and boundaries

Healthy listening is only the outer layer

Storage, indexing, and service health: use this distinction before changing durable state.

A process can listen while its configured provider, vector path, index, or durable store is degraded. Check in layers: process and loopback endpoint; resolved backend and database access; schema migration state; one bounded read/write; embedding or index freshness; provider readiness; then end-to-end recall.

Empty recall, code search, or document search is not by itself a health verdict. Confirm database identity, allowed root, feature gate, queue completion, index timestamp, and query mode before treating absence as corruption.

  • Observe before repairing.
  • Record the exact active database, not only DB_BACKEND input.
  • Use one synthetic probe and remove it.
  • Stop writers before copying SQLite or changing storage.
  • Let each index own its cleanup rows.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.storage-health.

Part IV / Chapter 1212.2 / understand

Concepts and boundaries

Retention is an active deletion policy

Storage, indexing, and service health: use this distinction before changing durable state.

Session pruning, agent-run pruning, artifact pruning, log pruning, and memory expiry are separate mechanisms. A zero or unset run-retention value can mean keep forever, while another subsystem may have its own default. Confirm each owner before promising preservation.

Workers run at boot and on timers. Shutdown must stop timers, scheduler, watchers, embedding work, sockets, model server, and database handles. A clean exit is part of data health because abandoned writers make later diagnosis ambiguous.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.storage-health.

Concepts and boundaries

Stored locally does not mean processed locally

Privacy and security boundaries: use this distinction before changing durable state.

Memory tier, storage backend, model provider, embedding provider, web or integration egress, file access, and retained artifacts are independent boundaries. Tier 3 is withheld from cloud recall; tier 2 is withheld by default or redacted when configured; tier 1 may be sent to the configured provider. Classify before storing, not after retrieval.

Local SQLite encryption protects the database file at rest with an OS-keychain key. It does not encrypt prompts already sent to a cloud provider, logs, exports, artifacts, model caches, Postgres, or another copy. Losing key access can make the encrypted database unavailable.

  • Use synthetic data for verification.
  • Grant the smallest read, write, credential, and tool scope.
  • Assume retrieved external content is untrusted.
  • Inspect exact confirmation payloads and reject unexpected scope.
  • Bound and redact retained evidence without destroying its diagnostic identity.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.privacy-security.

NON-RELEASE / Aperio 0.68.0 / Englishreview packet
NON-RELEASE
Part IV / Chapter 1313.2 / understand

Concepts and boundaries

A gate is not a sandbox

Privacy and security boundaries: use this distinction before changing durable state.

Allowed paths constrain product file tools, but a separately enabled shell runs host commands as the Aperio user. Provider sandboxes and client permissions are separate controls. Confirmation protects named mutations; it cannot make an overbroad credential or compromised host safe.

Secrets can leak through environment inheritance, process listings, logs, tool arguments, export files, and screenshots. Prefer secret stores supported by the deployment, avoid echoing values, and verify redaction with a fake token rather than a real one.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.privacy-security.

Concepts and boundaries

Portable export is not a full backup

Update, move, protect, recover, and uninstall: use this distinction before changing durable state.

The portable export contains memories and optionally wiki, agent jobs, agent runs, and self-memories. Import accepts memories, wiki articles, and self-memories, limits memories per request, and regenerates missing embeddings. That asymmetry alone prevents it from being a full round-trip backup.

A recoverable installation may also require schema and database contents, settings, encryption key access, indexed code/document state or a rebuild plan, session and run artifacts, credentials or re-entry plan, model and embedding dependencies, configuration, and the exact source release. Protect these according to backend while writers are stopped.

  • Inventory before copying.
  • Gracefully stop all writers.
  • Back up data and the means to decrypt and interpret it.
  • Restore into isolation and prove recall before changing the original.
  • Keep an exact rollback path until the new installation passes.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.lifecycle.

Update, move, recovery, and uninstall share one proof shape

Uninstall is deliberately last. Stop processes and triggers, export only what is wanted for portability, make and verify any required full backup, remove application code, then handle databases, volumes, caches, model weights, credentials, and keychain entries as separate explicit decisions.

Create and prove a recoverable installation backup

Audience

Goal and outcome
A full installation inventory is captured with backend-appropriate consistency, restored in isolation, and proven through fresh recall before the original is touched.
Prerequisites
Administrative access to the installation and its database; Enough separate storage for a backup and isolated restore; Access to required encryption keys without copying them into the manual evidence; A maintenance window to stop writers

Warning. Portable export/import is not this backup. Never copy a live SQLite file as the only backup, expose a key in logs, or test recovery over the original installation.

  2. Disable triggers and gracefully stop Aperio, MCP children, model processes, workers, watchers, and all database writers. Verify ports and handles are closed.

  3. Capture a backend-consistent database backup plus required configuration, artifact state, release identity, and a secure key-restoration plan. Hash and inventory the backup without publishing secrets.

Escalation does not broaden authority

Collect evidence and escalate: use this distinction before changing durable state.

A support request or issue body is data exchanged with another party. Do not attach databases, exports, credentials, full home-directory paths, private repository content, personal memories, or unrestricted logs unless a specific approved channel and necessity exist.

Part VI / Chapter 1919.1 / inspect

Evidence checklist

Escalation evidence packet

review before sharing

Observed

A bounded unresolved symptom needs another person or external dependency.

Least destructive checks first

A

Identity: release/SHA, interface, runtime/platform, backend/provider.

B

Reproduction: synthetic inputs, starting state, actions, expected/actual result.

C

Evidence: first bounded error, timestamps, relevant manifest hashes, cleanup result.

D

Safety: redacted credentials, paths, personal data, external content, and database material.

E

Scope: attempted checks, ruled-out layers, unavailable tools, and requested decision.

Recovery and verification

If redaction removes diagnostic meaning, replace sensitive values with stable labels and retain a private mapping; do not restore the secret. A second read can reproduce the issue and cannot recover a secret from the shared packet.

Reversal

Delete temporary unredacted copies and revoke any accidentally exposed credential.

Continue to the canonical procedure.

Concepts and boundaries

Reachable is not available, authorized, or safe

Tools, providers, integrations, and capability catalog: use this distinction before changing durable state.

A registered tool may reject because a feature is off, a path is outside scope, a credential is absent, a connection is read-only, a model lacks vision, or confirmation is pending. Those are distinct and useful outcomes.

Providers share orchestration goals but differ in credentials, tool schema translation, streaming, cancellation, and local/cloud data boundaries. One passing provider or interface does not verify another.

  • Start with discovery and read-only calls.
  • Apply least authority.
  • Inspect external egress and untrusted input.
  • Treat confirmation and cancellation as lifecycle states.
  • Record unavailable dependencies honestly.

Concepts and boundaries

Classify by owner and recovery method

Data, portability, and retention matrix: use this distinction before changing durable state.

Canonical records belong to the database; graph rows may be rebuildable from authorized roots; artifacts belong to sessions or runs; logs and caches are operational; credentials and keychain material have separate custody. A move or uninstall must decide each class explicitly.

Portable JSON is useful for selected logical records. Its export/import asymmetry, limits, missing settings/sessions/artifacts/keys, and embedding backfill make it unsuitable as the sole backup. Chapter 14 owns full recovery.

  • Stop writers before backend backup.
  • Preserve decryption ability separately and securely.
  • Verify imports by counts and recall.
  • Disable retention during evidence collection only when authorized.
  • Delete each class through its owner.

Canonical concept owned by chapter.data-portability.

Concepts and boundaries

Retention can preserve, expire, prune, or merely hide

Data, portability, and retention matrix: use this distinction before changing durable state.

Memory expiry excludes current recall but is not assured physical deletion. Session pruning, run pruning, artifact pruning, logs, and external-service retention use different clocks. A provider or integration may retain data beyond Aperio’s local cleanup.

State whether a row is durable, derived, transient, externally owned, or unknown; then attach its backup, restore, deletion, and verification method. Unknown must remain visible.

Use a term to find its owner

Part VII / Chapter 2525.2 / understand

Concepts and boundaries

Status words carry exact evidence limits

Glossary: use this distinction before changing durable state.

Verified means directly established against the pin and named evidence. Present-unverified means the surface exists but its complete support lane was not proven. Unsupported means absent or contradicted. Blocked names a required dependency or authority that is unavailable.

NON-RELEASE marks review material. It does not become a release because tests pass or filenames look final.

Glossary

Terms and distinctions

Field Console
TermMeaning in this manual
Affected flowThe user-visible path exercised after focused tests, including failure or cancellation and cleanup.
Agent jobA durable background-work definition; distinct from each run and gated separately from definition storage.
Allowed pathA symlink-aware product boundary authorizing specific file reads or writes; not a host sandbox.
AnamnesisRecall woven into thinking: Aperio’s design idea that durable memory should return as usable context and evidence.
ArtifactA generated or offloaded file owned by a session or run and governed by its retention and cleanup.
BackendThe active SQLite or Postgres store selected for durable product data.
BackupA backend-consistent, restorable protection set including every promised data class and required interpretation or key material.
Canonical ownerThe single source or procedure that defines a behavior; routes and summaries link to it rather than copy it.

Terms and distinctions

Field Console
TermMeaning in this manual
Confirmation interruptA server-owned pending decision binding a protected mutation to canonical arguments before execution.
ConversationThe active exchange with a model; it may be saved as a session but is not itself durable memory.
Evidence pinAn immutable product commit, blob, dependency digest, or approved artifact identity used to support a claim.
Fresh conversationA new conversation that does not receive the test value from prior chat turns; used to prove durable recall.
Generated factA read-only normalized row extracted from pinned authority with stable identity, status, source, and blob.
GraphA derived code-symbol or document-chunk projection of authorized roots; freshness and cleanup remain graph-specific.

MemoryA durable record intended for later recall, with identity, type, sensitivity, expiry, and version state.

25.1

Canonical procedure

Resolve a term to its canonical owner

An unfamiliar term is understood and routed to the chapter that owns its behavior.

Audience
Any reader
Goal and outcome
An unfamiliar term is understood and routed to the chapter that owns its behavior.
Prerequisites
The exact term or acronym; This offline glossary and index
Platform applicability
Terminology is platform-independent.

Warning. Do not execute an action from a glossary definition alone.

Starting state

Record the sentence and term whose meaning is unclear.

Actions

  1. Find the exact term or its expanded acronym in the glossary.

  2. Read the definition and note every explicit distinction.

  3. Use the full index to locate the canonical chapter, concept, or procedure.

  4. Read that owner’s applicability and warning before acting.

  5. If two definitions conflict, preserve both locations and treat the canonical owner as needing editorial reconciliation.

  6. Return to the original task with the owner and evidence boundary recorded.

The index routes; owners explain

Full index: use this distinction before changing durable state.

Entries use stable semantic identities and human labels. A destination may be a canonical procedure, concept, Field Console record, generated catalog row, or navigation route. Follow the destination for applicability and safety.

Generated fact families are indexed without reproducing all factual values here; the complete Field Console catalog remains searchable earlier in the book.

  • Pseudolocale paths remain internal QA only.
  • Index generation fails on broken destinations.

Search text first, then follow structure

Full index: use this distinction before changing durable state.

In HTML, use browser find and internal links. In PDF, use searchable text, bookmarks, and page navigation. Color, images, hover, animation, and network are never required.

If a link target is missing, that is a build defect. Do not compensate with an external URL or handwritten page number.

26.1

Canonical procedure

Find a task or concept offline

A term, symptom, command, capability, or procedure is found without network access.

Audience
Any reader
Goal and outcome
A term, symptom, command, capability, or procedure is found without network access.
Prerequisites
The English HTML or PDF artifact
Platform applicability
Search shortcut and PDF viewer vary; text and stable labels are common.

Warning. A search result is a route, not authority to run a command or approve a mutation.

Starting state

Choose the most specific noun, error fragment, stable ID, command, or outcome.

Actions

  1. Search the index text for the exact phrase, then a shorter stable noun.

  2. Choose the entry whose type and chapter match the task.

  3. Follow the internal link in HTML or use the labeled PDF destination.

  4. Read applicability, evidence status, and warning at the destination.

  5. Follow the canonical procedure or generated source link; do not act from the index label.

  6. Return through the destination’s next-task or role route.

NON-RELEASE review checklist

  • Cover is a complete Night Receiver page with the approved mascot and no unintended blank field.
  • Part openers use Night Receiver; ordinary interiors use Signal Desk; checklists, symptom records, matrices, glossary, index, and generated catalogs use Field Console.
  • “I want to...”, “Browse by topic”, four role routes, seven parts, and all 26 authored chapters are visible and usable.
  • Chapters 1-26 and back matter are understandable without color, images, mascot, hover, animation, or network.
  • No empty or fake reader-facing chapter page exists.
  • Canonical procedures show orientation, warning, starting state, actions, success, recovery, reversal, and next task.
  • Platform and interface lanes are shown only at genuine divergence and retain evidence labels.
  • Diagram, mascot, and v0.68.0-labeled facsimile are nonessential and semantically described.
  • A4 and Letter pages are readable in color and grayscale with no clipping or collisions.
  • This packet is reviewed only as NON-RELEASE; no publication, signing, revision, or release identity is approved.

What follows integration approval

  1. Continue authoring the remaining chapters in sequence; generated catalogs remain evidence inputs, never replacements for explanations or procedures.
  2. Run whole-book accessibility, link, print, pseudolocale, and release-readiness gates.
  3. Keep publication behind its later explicit human gate.

Stop. Approval authorizes canonical-source integration only. It does not authorize release filenames, checksums, signing, upload, publication, or alias movement.
